newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ERA uranium mine hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ERA uranium mine hit by strike.

text.p: Contract workers at the Ranger uranium mine in Australia's Northern Territory went on strike on Wednesday over health and safety claims, mine officials said.

The contractors were working on Ranger's expansion moves and uranium production, by fulltime staff, would not be affected, a spokesman for Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA), owner of the Ranger mine, told Reuters.
The strike was between several contract companies and their employees and did not directly involve ERA, ERA officials said.

Ken Lonie, general manager operations at Ranger, denied claims by strikers that contract workers were working in areas where Ranger employees were not allowed without a radiation detection badge. Contractors and staff emoployees all worked under the same conditions, he told Reuters.
The strike is also in support of enterprise bargaining and occupational health.
The strike involves 127 workers, members of the Construction, Forestry, Mining Energy Union (CFMEU) and the Electrical Trades Union.
The contract workers are building new milling plant at the Ranger mine.
Ranger's mill capacity is being boosted to 5,000 tonnes of uranium oxide a year from about 3,500 tonnes as part of a major expansion.
The strike will continue until a Thursday morning meeting by contract workers decides whether to continue the strike or to return to work.
